humanReviews.label: Reviewer mj9q
humanReviews.reviewText: The paper is practical and conceptually elegant, but the novelty beyond SVD-based methods is limited, the coefficient lacks theoretical grounding, and the soup terminology may overstate the relation to ensembling.

humanReviews.label: Reviewer YMQp
humanReviews.reviewText: The method is lightweight and empirically strong, but the single-checkpoint storage motivation is unconvincing and evidence on another modality such as audio would strengthen applicability.

humanReviews.label: Reviewer q1EA
humanReviews.reviewText: The coefficient interpretation is unclear, Figure 3 may conflict with the truncation narrative, gains over LiNeS are marginal without variability, generality may be regime-dependent, and Figure 2 has a pair-count discrepancy.

humanReviews.label: Reviewer gzvH
humanReviews.reviewText: The creative single-checkpoint reframing is strong, but plug-and-play practicality is qualified by selecting R, architecture diversity is limited, and a label-free selection rule is needed.

humanReviews.label: Reviewer Yqvj
humanReviews.reviewText: The method is simple and well motivated, but gains on strong checkpoints are modest, variability is missing, and the per-layer impact of the coefficients needs deeper analysis.

baselineReview.label: ChatGPT independent review
baselineReview.reviewText: An independent long-form review emphasizing coefficient semantics, signal dependence, update shrinkage, the Section 3-to-4 bridge, language effect-size arithmetic, SVD cost, aggregate CLIP statistics, and presentation accuracy.

themes.label: Contribution differentiation
themes.explanation: Both identify a contribution-positioning question; PeerMind abstains from external novelty adjudication.

themes.label: Weighting-rule theory
themes.explanation: All three reviews question the explanatory reach of the rule; PeerMind preserves its proven monotonicity and bounded sensitivity.

themes.label: Architecture and label-free evidence across versions
themes.explanation: The human concern was valid for the original submission snapshot. ConvNeXt and automatic-selection evidence added during rebuttal resolve the categorical absence only in the revised snapshot; documentation breadth remains limited.

themes.label: Language OOD protocol
themes.explanation: PeerMind isolates the distribution-shift definition separately from numerical language claims.

themes.label: Large-model scalability profile
themes.explanation: PeerMind and ChatGPT request quality and resource measurements at realistic model scale; PeerMind explicitly preserves the logical one-checkpoint savings.

themes.label: Figure 2 pair count
themes.explanation: Both identify the exact six-pair discrepancy; deterministic arithmetic verifies it.

themes.label: Effect size and uncertainty
themes.explanation: All three preserve large weak-checkpoint gains while requesting uncertainty and aggregate all-checkpoint statistics.

themes.label: Soup terminology
themes.explanation: A presentation/positioning issue not selected for the seven-finding PeerMind run.

themes.label: Storage-centered motivation
themes.explanation: A practical-premise judgment not independently checked.

themes.label: Audio modality coverage
themes.explanation: A useful extension rather than a demonstrated defect in the bounded vision/language evidence.

themes.label: Truncation narrative
themes.explanation: A graph-reading and regime-generality issue outside the selected seven findings.

themes.label: Notation and checkpoint documentation
themes.explanation: Human and ChatGPT reviews identify presentation problems outside the selected scientific investigations.

themes.label: Residual energy mislabeled as alignment
themes.explanation: All three identify the conceptual ambiguity; PeerMind resolves the exact identity and limits the verdict without rejecting the empirical CKA observation.

themes.label: Dependence among spectral signals
themes.explanation: PeerMind and ChatGPT identify the dependency; PeerMind avoids the stronger unsupported conclusion that the signals are completely redundant.

themes.label: Layer-wise shrinkage alternative
themes.explanation: PeerMind converts ChatGPT's strong hypothesis into a causal contract with a norm-matched scalar baseline and an explicit stop rule.

themes.label: Multi-model to single-model geometry bridge
themes.explanation: PeerMind and ChatGPT agree the quantities differ; PeerMind preserves the broader intuition and offers a wording-level falsifier or a substantive mapping.

themes.label: Claimed +9.2 language gains
themes.explanation: PeerMind turns the ChatGPT observation into a bounded table-to-text consistency check requiring exact calculation provenance.
